plan.title: KO x drug interaction DE in brain RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is a genotype x treatment interaction on a balanced 2x2 design (16 samples, 4 per cell) with a 12,000-gene raw count matrix (counts.csv) and a 16 x 4 sample table (metadata.csv) carrying genotype (WT, KO), treatment (vehicle, drug) and a combined condition column. The plan is therefore a single count-model track, not a set of pairwise comparisons.

T1S1 runs sample-structure QC on the raw counts: blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap and library sizes, coloured by genotype, treatment and cell. This must run before the model so a mis-assigned sample or a cell that separates for a non-biological reason is seen before any test. There is no batch column in metadata.csv, so no batch term can be fitted; if the PCA shows structure orthogonal to the design, that is reported as unexplained variance, not corrected.

T1S2 fits DESeq2 with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, reference levels set explicitly to WT and vehicle. The interaction coefficient (genotypeKO.treatmentdrug) is the direct answer to the question: the difference between the drug effect in KO and the drug effect in WT. Because DESeq2 also needs the simple effects to make the interaction interpretable, the step reports the drug-vs-vehicle effect in WT (the treatment main effect at the reference genotype) and in KO (main effect + interaction, extracted as a named contrast/list contrast), each with BH adjustment within the contrast and shrunken LFCs by ashr (the KO simple effect is a sum of coefficients, not a single coefficient, so apeglm cannot take it). Pre-filtering is minimal (>= 10 counts in >= 4 samples, the smallest cell size) so independent filtering at alpha 0.05 does the rest.

A caveat that shapes the reading of the whole plan: counts.csv is a gene-level table from salmon and the record does not state whether the length correction was applied, and there are no per-sample quant.sf files or an average-transcript-length table anywhere in the inputs. tximport cannot be run on a gene-level table. The model is therefore fitted on the counts as delivered with no length offset, and both T1S2 and T1S3 must state that the length offset is lost and that a shift in isoform usage can appear as differential expression.

T1S3 assembles the report: the three result sets side by side per gene (drug effect in WT, drug effect in KO, interaction), MA and dispersion plots, the p-value histogram per contrast inspected before adjustment, counts of NA p-values separated by cause (Cook's outlier flag versus independent filtering — with 4 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags rather than replaces outliers), and the reproducibility record. Power is the honest limitation: an interaction contrast is a difference of differences and 4 replicates per cell gives it a large standard error, so a small or empty interaction gene list is a statement about power as much as about biology, and the report says so.
